item.title: Yamal Makes History As Barça Ends Villa’s UCL Run
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jerome Miron Barcelona crushed Aston Villa 3-0 on Tuesday night in Spain, ending the English side’s perfect start to the UEFA Champions League. The rain poured down at Camp Nou, but that did not stop the home team from dominating the match. An error by João Gomes in the seventh minute allowed Lamine Yamal to score first. Yamal now holds the record as the competition’s top-scoring teenager with 14 total goals. He now holds the record that once belonged to Kylian Mbappé. Raphinha took over the game in the second half, scoring two more goals to seal the win. In only 13 appearances, he has accumulated 19 goals for this season. The victory puts Barcelona and Villa both at nine points in the standings, though Villa’s perfect record is now gone. This result shows the power of the young Spanish talent against a strong Premier League opponent. According to ESPN , the win helps Hansi Flick’s team regain momentum after losing two big games last month. A Historic Night for Youth The biggest story of the night belongs to the young winger who changed the history books. Yamal did not just score a goal; he broke a record that stood for years. He scored his 14th goal in the competition, surpassing the mark set by the French superstar Kylian Mbappé. This achievement highlights how quickly the new generation is taking over the sport. The Brazilian midfielder João Gomes made a costly mistake that led directly to the first goal. Yamal capitalized on that error with a trademark finish around the goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Barcelona’s press forced the error that gave them the lead. The rain made the field slick, but the young player found a way to score. He cut inside on his left foot and placed the ball perfectly past the helpless keeper. This moment proved that experience does not always beat raw talent and speed. The crowd at Camp Nou saw a future legend rise on a Tuesday night in November. Raphinha Leads the Attack Raphinha stepped up when the game mattered most in the second half. He has been playing as a striker under coach Hansi Flick since 2024, and his numbers show his value. His goal in the 52nd minute had a bit of luck, as the shot deflected past the keeper. The second goal, however, was a pure poacher’s finish following brilliant work from João Cancelo. According to ESPN, Raphinha has now scored 32 goals alongside Yamal out of Barcelona’s 60 total goals this season. These two players are the engine of the team. They have netted 32 of the team’s 60 goals in just 15 matches. Raphinha secured his seventh Champions League double, maintaining his lead as Europe’s top scorer across the top five leagues this season. His ability to play as a No. 9 has reached a new dimension this year. The Brazilian winger is proving he can carry the offensive load for the entire club. item.title: Knicks' Mike Brown makes stance on ex-Laker Dalton Knecht crystal clear after debut vs. Bulls
item.description: Knicks' Mike Brown makes stance on ex-Laker Dalton Knecht crystal clear after debut vs. Bulls originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This season has already been a rollercoaster for former Los Angeles Lakers first-round pick Dalton Knecht, and it hasn’t been long at all. Knecht was once considered the steal of the 2024 NBA Draft by Los Angeles. However, things have not gone according to plan after he saw limited playing time last season. The Lakers eventually ran out of plans for him, which is why they waived him before the season began to make room on the roster. “The Los Angeles Lakers are waiving 2024 No. 17 pick Dalton Knecht, sources tell ESPN,” ESPN’s Shams Charania wrote. Knecht became a highly sought-after free agent once he cleared waivers. After being one of the Lakers' best-kept secrets early in his career, he could become one of the team's biggest mistakes as time goes on. The former first-round pick ultimately decided to sign with the New York Knicks . “Former Lakers forward Dalton Knecht has agreed to sign with the New York Knicks on a two-way NBA contract, his agents at Excel Sports Management tell ESPN," Charania wrote. On Wednesday night, Knecht made his Knicks debut against the Chicago Bulls . The former Laker had a productive night off the bench, finishing with 10 points and seven rebounds. After the game, New York head coach Mike Brown made it clear that he views Knecht as a scorer, not just a shooter. “He's a scorer. He's not just a shooter. A lot of people think he's a shooter because he's white. I said it for you. I hope I don't get in trouble,” Brown told the media. There is no doubt that Brown made his thoughts on Knecht clear. Defensively, Knecht may still struggle at times, but he looked closer to his former self on offense. It was a great night for the Knicks all around, and Knecht took advantage of the opportunity in front of him. Brown clearly thinks highly of him as a scorer, so it will be interesting to see how Knecht's role evolves moving forward. item.title: Kane's Kompany pact! Striker salutes boss and opens up on bold decision to ditch Spurs comfort zone
item.description: Manchester City v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Harry Kane opened up on his strong working relationship with Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany following his contract extension until 2029. The striker also reflected on his choice to swap Premier League familiarity at Tottenham for a challenge in Germany. Perfect alignment between star striker and manager Harry Kane’s decision to commit his long-term future to FC Bayern reflects a strong tactical and mental alignment with manager Vincent Kompany. Since Kompany took charge, Kane has maintained his elite scoring rate while serving as a key leader in the dressing room. The striker revealed that Kompany allowed him total space and freedom when deciding his future. "He might have only found out this morning, I've not had any contact with him in the last few days! He never put pressure on me," Kane said. Respect for Kompany's relentless driving mentality Kane detailed how Kompany's coaching philosophy matches his own professional standards, regardless of a player's stature or experience. "We had an open chat about four weeks ago, but that was more general... I respect the coach a lot, the way he drives everyone," Kane explained. "Regardless of whether they've got 500 games under their belt or is new to the game. That's also my mentality, so we suit each other well." "I imagined challenging for the league, the cup and the Champions League every year... I've always believed in myself. Wherever I've played, I've scored goals," he added. Leaving Premier League comfort zone proved correct Reflecting on his departure from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023, Kane expressed zero regrets about leaving the English top flight to test himself abroad. "I spent a lot of time in the Premier League, I always watched them a lot. It's nice to have a change of scenery," Kane noted. "And sometimes a change is also good mentally... When I'm older, I'll look back and say this was the right step, to get out of my comfort zone." "The belief in yourself is an important factor. I feel as good as ever here. We'll be playing at the highest level in the next few years," the England captain affirmed. Kompany and Kane forge forward together With both manager and star forward aligned, Bayern look positioned to maintain a steady tactical foundation over the coming seasons. Kompany will rely on Kane's work ethic to drive the team's pressing structure and attacking fluidity. The pair now turn their full attention back to defending their domestic titles and challenging for European honors.

item.title: The Sabres’ Dylan Larkin Problem Isn’t the Assets
item.description: Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin has been suspended without pay since Oct. 29 , when he told the team he no longer wanted to be part of the organization, and a Dylan Larkin trade is still stuck behind the market he has limited himself to. He has given the Red Wings a list of 10 teams he would accept a deal to, and the Buffalo Sabres are not one of them. Why a Dylan Larkin trade to Buffalo is complicated Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic , who covers the Sabres, took a fan mailbag question Wednesday about whether Buffalo could get into the Larkin market at all. “But the Sabres are not on his expanded 10-team trade list. How much will that list have to expand before Buffalo ends up on it? Are the Sabres even a more attractive option than simply staying in Detroit? Yes, Buffalo ended its playoff drought, but that’s still just one year. Assuming he doesn’t want to go to a Canadian team, that leaves 26 teams. “I wonder if the Sabres would get on the list if it got to 15 teams? Would it take 20? And how much more would the Sabres have to pay for the Red Wings to be compelled to move him within the division? All of those questions make me hesitant to get people too excited about the idea. I also think the Sabres should be wary about adding a player who essentially needs to be begged to come to Buffalo. item.description: Brittney Griner lands unique role ahead of Unrivaled’s third season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Brittney Griner's legendary WNBA career is winding down. Sure, Griner is still capable of dropping 25 points on any given night, and she's still capable of dominating defensively as the WNBA's active leader in blocks per game. But the fact is, Griner turned 36 last month, and the forthcoming 2027 season -- where she will return home to Texas as a member of the rebooted Houston Comets -- is almost certain to be her last in The W. MORE : Olivia Miles brings buzz to Unrivaled amid Hive roster reveal Griner's role in Unrivaled for the upcoming season serves as some confirmation that the nine-time All-Star is actively preparing for the next phase of her career in basketball. Griner will receive mentorship in this department from Unrivaled's head coaches, as well as "hands-on" coaching experience. The wheels were put in motion for Griner's transition into coaching during the 2026 season in Connecticut, where Griner sat in on film sessions in a sort of "coaching internship" role. item.title: Five Reasons Nebraska Will Win: Illinois
item.description: Well, it’s November. The Huskers are 5-3 and just need one more win to once again become bowl eligible. Some of you may have counted them out after the soul crushing path these last few games have led us down, but I haven’t! This week is about redemption. This week the Huskers are going to come out on fire and cruise their way to win number six. These are your reasons why: #1 THE DEFENSE The Husker defense has been the backbone of this team. They are the reason that the Huskers were still in the game and ahead in the fourth quarter in each of the last three games. This defense will be sharp against a balanced Illinois attack and will be ready to cause some takeaways. #2 RUNNING ROOM Nebraska has not seen a lot of offense in the last three games. They’ve been low scoring and aside from a couple drives the Huskers have found it hard to move the ball. That changes this week. The offensive line is going to get a good push on the Illini defense and will give the running backs plenty of running room. Also, for the Huskers to win, we are going to need to see more of Jamal Rule on the field. Isaiah Mozee and Mekhi Nelson do fine, but the rushing game was so much stronger with Rule leading the pack. #3 Anthony Colandrea Anthony Colandrea has been leading this team. He has done all he can to get this team to win. Last week was a rough one for him, he threw three interceptions. I think it’s hard to always blame the quarterback for those, when part of the problem is receivers not running the routes that they need to be. Regardless of last week, Colandrea will be back on that field and he will be ready to lead this Husker team to a victory. He will be ready and we will be cheering for him as he dashes down field for a Husker touchdown. #4 THE RULE OF THREES Good and bad things come in threes. Illinois is on a three game winning streak, Nebraska is on a three game losing streak. Now that they have both accomplished those tasks in threes, they must switch and go the other direction. Therefore, Nebraska will win and Illinois will lose. It’s basic science and math really. #5 IT’S FRIDAY NIGHT Nebraska and Illinois are playing on a Friday night for their third consecutive meeting. The Huskers won the first game in 2023 20-7, Illinois won the second game 31-24 in overtime. It is only logical then that the Huskers will win the third one. You know, because they are trading every other win. It’s something a polite team would do and I know Illinois is nothing if they aren’t polite. item.title: Confirmed: Seven Barcelona academy players named in Spain U17 World Cup squad
item.description: Confirmed: Seven Barcelona academy players named in Spain U17 World Cup squad As many as seven Barcelona youth talents will be a part of the Spain national team squad at the upcoming U17 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Indeed, manager David Cubillo has called up seven exciting La Masia talents in the form of Raul Exposito, Sergi Mayans, Baba Kourouma, Jordi Pesquer, Ebrima Tunkara, Roberto Tomas and Iu Martinez. Of the seven players, four happen to be defenders: Exposito, Mayans, Kourouma, and Pesquer, who has already had some experience in the first-team dynamics, having participated in the pre-season during the summer. Meanwhile, Tunkara, who continues to be called up to first-team training regularly, and Roberto Tomas will be the midfielders representing Barça at the U17 World Cup with Spain. Iu Martinez is the only forward from La Masia to be called up for the tournament. The seven Barça players will report for the training camp in Madrid on 9 November before flying to Qatar for the tournament. As such, they will miss an important stretch of matches with the club’s youth and reserve teams. Spain have been drawn in Group H, along with Morocco, Fiji, and China. Having never won the U17 World Cup, they will be eager to follow in the footsteps of the senior national team and the U15 side and lift the trophy.

item.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Tight End Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Kyle Pitts vs. Brenton Strange
item.description: Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. (8) catches a five-yard touchdown pass against the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Not every fantasy football manager is lucky enough to start one of the elite TEs each week. Kyle Pitts Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. (8) celebrates after a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Pitts was limited to only 2.6 fantasy points in Week 8, but that was against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a far-from-ideal weather game. Additionally, between Pitts and Strange, Pitts has the higher touchdown upside. Strange has caught just one touchdown this season, and he has an unreliable role in the red zone, despite being in the better offensive environment. While the Jaguars are favored on the road against the shorthanded Ravens on Thursday Night Football, Strange may not see much usage. Jacksonville has three blowout wins this year, and Strange has scored fewer than 10 fantasy points in two of them. Both Pitts and Strange are viable starters for fantasy football managers in Week 9, but Pitts carries a higher ceiling. item.title: Sack-Prone Texas Offense Could Reignite Mizzou Pass Rush
item.description: Mizzou’s defense made it look relatively easy to get to the quarterback through the first half of the season. Over the past two weeks, however, the Tigers have struggled to generate the same pressure, giving the Texas offense an opportunity to exploit its pass-protection vulnerabilities. After 18 sacks through the first six games, Mizzou has managed just one over its last two contests. The Tigers have also totaled just three tackles for loss and seven quarterback hurries during that stretch. The recent production dip has dropped Mizzou to 11th in the SEC in total sacks. Despite the decrease, defensive ends Daeden Hopkins and Donta Simpson remain among the conference’s top five sack leaders with seven and six, respectively. Neither has maintained that production recently. Hopkins has gone without a sack in the last two games and recorded just one quarterback hurry. Simpson has added one sack and two hurries during that span. The bigger concern for the Tigers has been generating consistent pressure off the edge. Of the Tigers’ 19 sacks this season, nine have come from defensive tackles, 8.5 from defensive ends and 1.5 from linebacker Nic Rodriguez. Last season, Damon Wilson II and Zion Young combined for 15.5 sacks as edge rushers, providing a tandem of production that Mizzou has yet to replicate. Injuries have played a significant role. Hopkins has missed two games, Simpson was unavailable against Mississippi State and Darris Smith, who entered the season as the projected leader off the edge after recording four sacks in 2025, has appeared in just four games while playing fewer than 150 snaps. Smith did see an increased workload against Arkansas, recording 38 snaps, his most since playing 56 against Kansas. The lack of production hasn’t necessarily reflected a lack of creativity from defensive coordinator Corey Batoon and his staff. Against Arkansas, Mizzou mixed four- and five-man fronts with disguised coverages. item.description: PEORIA — Claire McDougall loves basketball. But unfortunately, the Bradley Braves guard/forward will spend her senior women's basketball season on the sidelines. item.title: Why does the BYU-Utah rivalry game trigger such deep emotions? We asked a sports psychology professor
item.description: Eliza Anderson, Deseret News As you’re settling in Saturday morning for the BYU versus Utah kickoff, consider a question that fans have likely been asking since the gladiators battled in the Roman Colosseum over 2,000 years ago: “Why are many of us so emotionally invested in the outcome of a game being played by young athletes that most don’t know?” There’s no rational answer to that query. Unless you’re a gambler, the final score in Saturday’s Cougars/Utes contest won’t affect your bankbook. The Big Game results won’t move gas prices. Taxes aren’t going away. And your golf handicap? Sorry, it stays the same. But forget rationality. The outcome of the annual Red-and-Blue rivalry game matters deeply to many of us. When the final horn blows, legions of fans sporting one particular color will be celebrating. And legions wearing the other color will be grumbling. And the number of postgame “celebrators” and the “grumblers” will be almost evenly split, according to a new poll released Thursday. When 786 Utahns were asked in a recent Y2 Analytics survey which Utah school they usually root for, BYU edged out the University of Utah 37% to 34%, with the remainder of respondents claiming support for other teams or no team from the Beehive State. But when all participating in the survey were required to pick a side — BYU or Utah — roughly 52% of respondents sided with the Utes, compared to 48% for the Cougs. Why do we care so much about a college football game? The Deseret News reached out to Matt Moore, a sports and exercise psychology professor at the University of Utah who has worked with both schools, to explore why many care so deeply about the annual Cougars-Utes football game. Moore’s simple answer: It’s vital to many Utahns’ identity. “We are social beings that walk through this world with identities: ‘I work here,’ or ‘I go to school here,’ or ‘I live here,’ or ‘I own this,’ or ‘I cheer for this team,’ or ‘I belong to this faith/religion’,” he wrote in an email. Psychology’s Social Identity Theory comes into play when examining fans of both teams, he added. The teams we attach our personal identity to become part of the larger “Us” — our school, family, faith tradition, history and community. “That is why fans say, ‘ We won,’ rather than, ‘ They won,’ even though 99% of fanbases haven’t even stepped foot on the field or inside a locker room,” explained Moore. “Team success can bring genuine pride, belonging, and joy. item.description: Stephen Welsh has started 13 of Swansea's 14 league games so far this season [PA] Swansea City have received a major fitness boost after influential centre-back Stephen Welsh was cleared of serious injury. Swansea feared the Scotland international had suffered knee ligament damage following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Tuesday's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth. But scans have revealed Welsh has no significant problem, meaning he may even be able to play some part at Birmingham City on Saturday. There is more positive news from the treatment room going into the weekend, with wingers Moussa Yeo and Eom Jisung fit to return against Chris Davies' in-form Blues side. However, midfielder Stephen Eustaquio will again be absent due to a groin problem and Melker Widell is out with a minor hamstring injury which meant he was withdrawn at half-time at Fratton Park. "Welshy's scan is clear. It's just really a bad knock so there's nothing major," said Swansea head coach Vitor Matos. "We will still assess if he will be available for Saturday, but it's not a bad injury. It's just a knock that is really, really painful." Matos says a decision is yet to be taken on whether Welsh, 26, will join up with Scotland in the international break which follows the Birmingham game. item.title: Is a sports media blue wave coming, too?
item.description: Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect This originally appeared in Thursday morning’s edition of The A Block, Awful Announcing’s daily newsletter with the latest sports media news, commentary, and analysis. Sign up here to be the first to know everything happening in the sports media world each day. Only a fool would try to extrapolate what happened on election night and tell you what’s next. While I am a fool, I will refrain from doing so. Instead, I’ll ponder a question. Will the ripple effects from Tuesday’s Blue Tsunami make their way to the sports media world? I ask because we’re only two years removed from seeing how shifting political headwinds can affect the industry and its content. This political outcome didn’t happen overnight. We can debate the specific reasons, but the person at the center of this seismic change is Donald Trump, and America’s desire to pull away or move past him has been months in the making. I think about that when I look around at the state of the sports media world and how some of the things he affected or influenced are already fraying at the edges. The Vibe Shift That Wasn’t Remember the Trump Vibe Shift ? That sense that, as David Wallace-Wells put it , “the country would be moving MAGA-ward — both in politics and beyond it.” We saw it in the ways sports leagues changed their policies and even their histories to appease a new cultural worldview. We saw it with the mainstream acceptance of Barstool Sports and Pat McAfee’s world domination . LIV Golf’s presumed domination thanks to Saudi backing and Trump approval. item.title: Long climb to the top: Inside Guilderland girls' tennis' historic state semifinal run
item.description: Guilderland tennis teammates Meghan Uzzilia, left, and Angela Li during the Section 2 finals against Niskayuna on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Schenectady, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) GUILDERLAND CENTER - Guilderland's grind to reach the top of the Section 2 Class AA girls' tennis hierarchy proved to be a methodical push up from the middle of the pack. But longtime Lady Dutch Coach Deb Murray had an inkling heading into this fall that her 2026 squad was ready to break through. "I knew that this would be the year to do it if we were going to make it happen," Murray said. "I have five seniors that have been with me since they were 11 and 12 years old. It is an exceptional group. They have been committed to the game and with me on the varsity. They play in the seven main positions. Last year, we were good. We beat Saratoga Springs during the regular season and lost to them in the final." Guilderland not only edged Shaker 5-4 for the sectional title, but has since won two more matches to advance to the Division I state semifinals Friday at the United States Tennis Association's Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing. Guilderland faces Section 1 champion Horace Greeley at 9:30 a.m. If the Section 2 champion prevails, it would compete in the title match in the afternoon. "I have been waiting for something like this since I joined the team," said senior Angela Li, who became a member of the varsity roster in eighth grade. "I never expected it. I have played tennis all my life and Guilderland tennis gave me a new opportunity. I have really enjoyed it on this team." "I am excited. No matter how well we do, we got there," Guilderland senior Meghan Uzzilia said. "This is the first time a Guilderland team has done this and there are also not many teams from around the state that have been this far." Guilderland's first sectional title in 16 years was followed up by a 7-0 triumph over Queensbury for the right to represent Section 2 in the state Division I tournament. They followed with a 6-1 regional victory over Section 3 champion Fayetteville-Manlius. Players say they were motivated to win the title for Murray because of all the work she's put in through the years. "It meant a lot to us to get her that win," Uzzilia said. "We had never been to regionals before and it was nice to play new people." "We were all really happy to win it. We felt we deserved it after what happened last year, coming in second at sectionals," Li said. "This is the best team Guilderland has had in a while now. It is a great opportunity to be on this team now." The last time Guilderland captured a sectional team title in 2010, there was no team state championship event to compete in. "Because we were so close last year, we knew we had to pull this off this year," Uzzilia said. "Our lineup pretty much stayed the same and we have a pretty strong team. I had a lot of confidence going into the season. I really thought we would take the whole thing."

item.title: Cubs free agent target: Freddy Peralta
item.description: Right-hander Freddy Peralta was widely assumed to be a Cubs trade target last summer while he was with the Mets. He’d had several good seasons pitching for Craig Counsell in Milwaukee, likely enough to recommend him. But Peralta was pretty bad in 22 starts with the Mets: 4.99 ERA, 1.478 WHIP, 17 home runs allowed in 113.1 innings. That included losing twice to the Cubs. So the Cubs instead traded for two other members of the Mets rotation and Peralta went to the Rays, where he pitched in the World Series — and was also very good in the 10 regular-season starts he made in Tampa Bay, posting a 3.25 ERA and 1.012 WHIP, more in line with his Milwaukee numbers The reason this happened is simple. The Rays figured out how to fix him: [Jorge] Moncada, the Rays’ bullpen coach since 2023 after a lengthy stint in their system as a pitching coach and coordinator, dug into video of Peralta when he was at his best for Milwaukee last September and when he was at his worst in his final starts as a Met in July. Soon enough, Moncada noticed something: Last season, Peralta exclusively pitched out of the stretch. This season, he was going through an elaborate windup, hands over his head, with the bases empty. So he posed a question to his newest pupil as the meeting drew to a close: Which is more comfortable? “He said, ‘I always feel comfortable pitching out of the stretch,'” Moncada said. “So we were like, ‘Go with what makes you most comfortable,’ and he went back.” From there, the Rays instituted further modifications. They had Peralta move to the third-base side of the rubber and widen his stance. They told him to speed up his delivery. They gave him a drill package to incorporate into his preparation to generate more strength from his legs. In one of the drills, Peralta straps a 3D belt around his waist and Moncada pulls it so he feels the weight in his backside. The modified routine, Moncada explained, set the foundation for Peralta to create better momentum toward the plate. His arm angle was raised slightly. His average arm extension rose a fraction. I quoted quite a bit there — and there’s more, go to the link — mainly to give a prime example of how other teams’ pitching infrastructure is so far superior to the Cubs’. I wonder, had the Cubs actually been able to trade for Peralta, whether they would have been able to figure these things out and implement them the way they were in Tampa Bay. I’ll continue to maintain that Jed Hoyer ought to fire pitching coach Tommy Hottovy, VP of pitching strategy Tyler Zombro, and the rest of the pitcher coaches and start over. How much worse could it be? Nevertheless, it does appear that Peralta is back to the way he pitched in Milwaukee, and that should be something that should attract the Cubs to signing him, especially with his long history with Counsell.
